title: Exposure to natural disasters and vaccination indicators: a systematic review and directions for future research.
authors: Shea B, Shaman J
abstract: Global routine childhood immunization has stagnated for almost two decades, leaving children vulnerable to both immediate and long-term health risks from infectious diseases. Identifying and mitigating impediments to childhood vaccination, such as barriers resulting from exposure to natural disasters, is vital for maintaining population health. While there is general understanding that disasters have the potential to disrupt vaccination services, well designed studies on the degree to which exposure to natural disasters affects vaccination indicators are limited. Understanding the effects of natural disasters on vaccine preventable diseases is an important area for future research as some natural disasters are becoming more frequent and intense due to climate change. To understand the current state of research on exposure to natural disasters and vaccination indicators (i.e., vaccination metrics including administration, coverage, rates), we conducted a systematic literature review of all literature in Embase, Google Scholar, PubMed, and Web of Science up until September 11-12, 2025. We aimed to identify relevant peer reviewed literature focusing on natural disasters and immunization and to assess them for relevance and inclusion. Seventeen studies met the criteria for inclusion. These studies examined the relationship between exposure to cyclones/hurricanes, droughts, earthquakes, flooding, heat waves, and multiple disaster types and changes in vaccination among different age groups. Most (16/17 (94.12%)) papers identified a connection or association between exposure to natural disasters and reduced vaccination indicators. The majority (13/17 (76.47%)) of studies focused on early-childhood vaccinations. Characteristics that affect vulnerability to under-vaccination-exposure level, geographical location, socioeconomic status-were assessed in several papers. Areas for future research include quantifying the degree to which different disaster types affect multiple vaccination indicators within the same individuals and changes in communities over time.

title: H-shaped sponge positioner prevents pressure injuries during prolonged prone ventilation in acute respiratory distress syndrome: a single-center, open-label, randomized controlled trial.
authors: Wang Y, Liu J, Chen S, Tian S, Hu S, Tang B, Zeng L, Luo L
abstract: In patients with moderate-to-severe acute respiratory distress syndrome, prolonged prone position ventilation is frequently employed to enhance oxygenation but often results in pressure injuries. To protect patients from such injuries, a new H-shaped sponge locator was designed in the study. In this single-center, open-label, randomized controlled trial, 60 patients with moderate-to-severe acute respiratory distress syndrome requiring extended prone position ventilation (≥ 12 hours per session) were recruited from the General Intensive Care Unit at Xiangtan Central Hospital, Hunan Province, China, between May 2023 and May 2024. Participants were randomly allocated to either the intervention group, which received prone positioning with the assistance of the H-shaped sponge positioner, or the control group, which used conventional soft pillows for support. The primary outcomes included the number of anatomical sites affected by pressure injuries and injury severity, classified according to the revised 2016 National Pressure Ulcer Advisory Panel/the European Pressure Ulcer Advisory Panel staging criteria. Secondary outcomes included mean airway pressure, oxygenation index (PaO2/FiO2), intravesical pressure, and the frequency of support device adjustments. Data from 29 patients in each group were analyzed. Significant group × time interactions were observed for both the number of pressure injury sites and overall incidence. Although pressure injuries increased progressively across all sessions in both groups, patients in the intervention group consistently had fewer injury sites. There were no significant group × time interactions for mean airway pressure or intravesical pressure. However, both measures increased over time in all patients, with significantly lower values in the intervention group. Oxygenation index improved over time, with no statistically significant differences between groups. The intervention group required markedly fewer support device adjustments. In patients with moderate-to-severe acute respiratory distress syndrome receiving extended prone position ventilation, the H-shaped sponge positioner significantly outperformed standard soft pillow support in preventing pressure injuries. This cost-efficient device not only minimized the number and severity of pressure ulcers but also reduced mean airway and intra-abdominal pressures and decreased the frequency of nursing interventions. Given its ease of use and affordability, the H-shaped positioner holds substantial promise for clinical application, particularly in resource-constrained settings, and warrants further evaluation in broader implementation studies. This trial was registred at National Health Security Information Platform (Medical Research Registration and Information System, https://www.medicalresearch.org.cn, Registration No. MR-43-23-039592) on March 30, 2023.

title: Nucleic acid amplification testing for obligate intracellular and cell wall-deficient bacteria: from assay performance to clinical interpretation, a structured narrative review.
authors: Naderi M, Sadidi R, Besharati R, Kebriae A, Azimian A
abstract: Obligate intracellular bacteria (Rickettsia, Orientia, Ehrlichia, Anaplasma, Coxiella, Chlamydia) and cell wall-deficient Mycoplasma species present profound diagnostic challenges due to their fastidious growth, low circulating burden, and genomic instability. Nucleic Acid Amplification Tests (NAATs) have revolutionized detection, yet critical gaps persist in distinguishing active infection from persistent DNA, standardizing cycle threshold interpretation, and integrating host-response biomarkers. This structured narrative review provides a comprehensive analysis of the complete diagnostic armamentarium for these pathogens. It is based on a reproducible, non-systematic literature survey and is not a PRISMA-compliant systematic review. We cover conventional methods (culture, serology), NAAT platforms (qPCR, digital PCR, isothermal amplification), and emerging technologies including CRISPR-Cas diagnostics, metagenomic sequencing, nanopore sequencing, biosensors, and host-response biomarker profiling. We introduce four conceptual frameworks: the "biological noise" paradigm reframing low-copy detection as a signal-to-noise challenge; a temporal-dynamic algorithm accounting for pathogen-specific detection windows; the "detection-disease disconnect" emphasizing clinical contextualization of NAAT positivity; and multi-analyte integration combining NAAT with viability markers and host inflammatory signatures. We also position these frameworks relative to prior diagnostic-interpretation theories, including STARD, QUADAS-2, MIQE, Bayesian pretest-posttest reasoning, Ct-value interpretation guidance, and host-response classifier frameworks. We compare ten clinically significant pathogens across technical and biological parameters, evaluate point-of-care deployment strategies, and address antimicrobial resistance testing. Performance metrics are presented as context-dependent estimates rather than fixed constants. The next frontier lies not in incremental assay improvements but in system-level integration of pathogen detection, viability assessment, host-response profiling, and clinical phenotyping, supported by artificial intelligence-enhanced interpretation and global standardization efforts.

title: Low-dose carbon monoxide in cardiovascular surgery: mechanisms, monitoring, and therapeutic potential.
authors: Zou J, Wang J, Wang T, Zhang H, Zhang J, Ji B
abstract: Carbon monoxide has been regarded as a toxic gas for a long time, however, recent studies have demonstrated that carbon monoxide, as an endogenous gaseous signaling molecule generated via the heme oxygenase system, plays an important regulatory role in various physiological and pathological processes. Physiologically, endogenous carbon monoxide production is approximately 400-500 μmol per day, whereas freely diffusible carbon monoxide remains very low, at about 0.002 μM, or approximately 2.5 ppm as an equivalent gas-phase concentration. At low concentrations, carbon monoxide exerts diverse biological effects, including anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, anti-apoptotic, vasoregulatory, mitochondrial-modulating, and anti-remodeling actions. These properties are particularly relevant to cardiovascular surgery, especially procedures involving cardiopulmonary bypass, where systemic inflammation, ischemia-reperfusion injury, hemolysis, endothelial dysfunction, and microcirculatory disturbance contribute substantially to perioperative morbidity. During cardiopulmonary bypass, endogenous carbon monoxide production may increase and can be indirectly assessed by carboxyhemoglobin and exhaled carbon monoxide, suggesting a potential role for carbon monoxide-related measurements as dynamic biomarkers of hemolysis, inflammation, and surgical stress. In parallel, preclinical studies have shown that low-dose inhaled carbon monoxide and carbon monoxide-releasing molecules may alleviate inflammatory responses, preserve mitochondrial function, protect the vascular endothelium, and reduce cardiovascular surgery-related organ injury under controlled experimental conditions. Nevertheless, the translational application of carbon monoxide remains limited by its narrow therapeutic window, dose- and time-dependent biological effects, interindividual variability, and the need for rigorous perioperative monitoring. This review summarizes the sources, metabolism, molecular targets, and cardiovascular effects of carbon monoxide, with a focus on its monitoring value and therapeutic potential in cardiovascular surgery. We further discuss current evidence, safety considerations, and future directions for translating low-dose carbon monoxide and carbon monoxide-releasing strategies into perioperative cardiovascular care.

title: Environmental microbial exposure as an under-measured exposome domain: Links to host microbiomes, immune regulation, and disease epidemiology.
authors: Parekh Y, Parmar V
journal: Journal of environmental health science & engineering
abstract: Environmental microbial exposure is an under-measured biological component of the exposome and a plausible determinant of immune-mediated disease patterns. Humans encounter microbial communities and products from soil, air, water, vegetation, animals, food systems, farms, indoor dust, healthcare settings, schools, and urban built environments. These exposures may influence gut, skin, airway, oral, and mucosal microbiomes and thereby alter epithelial barrier function, immune tolerance, inflammatory thresholds, and microbial metabolite production. This structured mechanistic narrative review integrates direct environmental-exposure studies, environment-to-host microbiome studies, host-microbiome mechanistic evidence, and translational frameworks. The clearest convergence occurs in asthma and allergic disease, where early-life farm exposure, endotoxin-rich dust, environmental microbial diversity, innate immune modulation, and epithelial A20 regulation support a coherent exposure-response model. Evidence for inflammatory bowel disease and broader respiratory outcomes is biologically credible but less direct, whereas metabolic and systemic inflammatory outcomes remain largely supported by host-microbiome and metabolite mechanisms rather than direct environmental exposure studies. The review therefore distinguishes evidence maturity and mechanistic proximity rather than treating all disease categories equally. It further positions pollution, urbanization, building design, biodiversity loss, diet, antibiotics, and socioeconomic conditions as active modifiers of microbial exposure and host response. Future studies should integrate direct environmental sampling with body-site microbiome profiling, functional multi-omics, immune and barrier biomarkers, geospatial exposure assessment, source tracking, repeated measures, and explicit causal-inference designs. Environmental microbial exposure should be treated neither as uniformly beneficial nor harmful, but as a measurable, context-dependent exposome domain whose health effects depend on composition, dose, timing, route, co-exposures, and host susceptibility.

title: Kidney effects of inhaled nitric oxide in critically ill patients: from pathophysiological considerations to clinical implications.
authors: Robert A, Gonze A, Bulpa P, Hauquiert B
abstract: Inhaled nitric oxide is widely used as a selective pulmonary vasodilator in critical care, yet its renal effects remain controversial. While existing reviews mostly focus on indications for inhaled nitric oxide and its impact on outcomes, limited data exist on its renal effects, since it was thought to act only locally in the lungs. This review examine the clinical evidence regarding kidney outcomes associated with inhaled nitric oxide across major indications and provide an integrated mechanistic analysis of nitric oxide signaling in renal physiology and pathophysiology. Nitric oxide is produced by nitric oxide synthases using L-arginine as a substrate. It acts as a smooth muscle relaxation factor and ultimately causes vasodilation through its effect on cyclic guanosine monophosphate. Nitric oxide plays a pivotal role in renal hemodynamic regulation, glomerular filtration, tubular function, and microcirculatory homeostasis. The net renal effect of inhaled nitric oxide likely reflects the balance between improved nitric oxide signaling and oxidative stress generation. Available clinical data suggest that the renal impact of inhaled nitric oxide is context-dependent. In acute respiratory distress syndrome, higher-level evidence indicates a potential increase in acute kidney injury, possibly related to oxidative and nitrosative stress. Conversely, in cardiac bypass surgery, inhaled nitric oxide may confer nephroprotection by restoring nitric oxide bioavailability during hemolysis and free hemoglobin-mediated nitric oxide scavenging. In other conditions, including organ transplantation, pulmonary hypertension, sepsis, and hemolytic disorders, evidence remains limited or inconclusive. Overall, current evidence does not support a uniform renal effect of inhaled nitric oxide, indicating the need for prospective studies with predefined renal endpoints to clarify its clinical relevance.

title: Gegen qinlian decoction alleviates DSS-induced colitis through modulation of intestinal stem cell homeostasis and M1 macrophage polarization.
authors: Wang M, Yang X, Ji N, Wang X, Cheng Y, Liu Z, Ren L, Leng Z
abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) imposes a significant burden on human health and socioeconomic systems. Gegen Qinlian Decoction (GQD) is an effective formula clinically used for the treatment of IBD. However, the underlying mechanisms of GQD in treating colitis remain incompletely elucidated. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to investigate the therapeutic effects of GQD in DSS-induced colitis mice, and explore the underlying mechanisms, thereby providing novel perspectives and strategies for colitis treatment. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A mouse colitis model was induced by administering 2.5% dextran sulfate sodium (DSS) in drinking water. The therapeutic efficacy of GQD was assessed by monitoring body weight, disease activity index (DAI), colon length, histopathological damage, inflammatory cytokines, and intestinal mechanical and mucus barrier function. RNA sequencing was performed to reveal the underlying mechanisms. The effects of GQD on macrophage polarization and intestinal stem cells (ISCs) restoration were subsequently examined. RESULTS: GQD treatment significantly alleviated DSS-induced colitis and tissue damage, accompanied by restoration of tight junction protein expression and improvement of mucus barrier function. RNA sequencing suggested that the effects of GQD in colitis mice were closely associated with ISCs and macrophage functions. Experimental validation demonstrated that GQD treatment was associated with increased expression of ISC-associated markers, including AXIN2, and improved goblet cell-associated mucus barrier parameters. Meanwhile, GQD treatment attenuated M1 macrophage polarization, accompanied by decreased inflammatory cytokine levels and alleviation of intestinal inflammation. These effects were also accompanied by reduced SNX10 expression and alterations in Wnt/β-catenin and NLRP3/caspase-1 signaling pathways. CONCLUSION: GQD ameliorates intestinal mucosal barrier function and promotes mucosal healing in DSS-induced colitis mice. These effects are associated with the upregulation of ISC-related markers expression and the inhibition of M1 macrophage polarization.

title: Engineering a PEG/Co-modified carbon paste electrode for highly sensitive voltammetric determination of ophthalmic antihistamine epinastine: From pharmaceutical analysis to ocular pharmacokinetics.
authors: Al-Khateeb LA, Gamal M, Hussein OG
abstract: Rapid and highly sensitive monitoring of epinastine in pharmaceutical formulations and biological matrices remains a significant analytical challenge, demanding methods that combine simplicity, affordability, and excellent analytical performance. In this study, a polyethylene glycol/cobalt-modified carbon paste electrode (PEG/Co/CPE) was fabricated as a novel electrochemical sensing platform for epinastine determination. The combined incorporation of PEG and Co enhanced the electrochemical response through increased electrochemically accessible surface area and modified interfacial characteristics while scan-rate studies indicated predominantly diffusion-controlled epinastine oxidation. Following systematic optimization of the experimental conditions, the proposed square wave voltammetric method exhibited two linear concentration ranges of 20.0-1400.0 nM and 2.0-100.0 μM with excellent correlation coefficients (r = 0.9998 and 0.9997, respectively). The sensor demonstrated remarkable sensitivity achieving a limit of detection of 6.5 nM and a limit of quantification of 19.8 nM. Method validation confirmed excellent analytical reliability with recoveries of 99.84 ± 0.71% and 100.26 ± 0.65% while repeatability and intermediate precision showed relative standard deviation values below 1.5%. The method was successfully applied to the determination of epinastine in a commercial ophthalmic formulation affording a recovery of 99.72 ± 0.58% whereas the standard-addition procedure yielded a mean recovery of 99.85 ± 0.11% indicating negligible matrix interference. In rabbit aqueous humor, the bioanalytical assay displayed linearity over 20.0-1400.0 nM with r = 0.9998, a detection limit of 6.3 nM, and a quantification limit of 19.1 nM while satisfying accepted criteria for accuracy, precision, and stability. Furthermore, the validated sensor enabled successful pharmacokinetic profiling following ocular administration providing reliable estimates of Cmax (27.20 ng/mL), Tmax (4.0 h), and elimination half-life (5.59 h). Collectively, the developed sensor provides a robust, cost-effective, and high-performance electroanalytical platform with strong potential for routine pharmaceutical quality control and bioanalytical pharmacokinetic applications.

title: Ulcerative colitis imaging via a ratiometric fluorescent probe with large emission shift for SO2 sensing.
authors: Long S, Gao S, Liu Y, Zhang J, Shi H, Wang A, Zhang Y, Chen W
abstract: Sulfur dioxide (SO2) serves as a gaseous signaling molecule that exerts pivotal regulatory functions in diverse physiological and pathological processes and has emerged as a novel gaseous biomarker associated with multiple inflammatory and hepatic diseases. Ulcerative colitis (UC), a diffuse inflammatory bowel disease primarily affecting the colonic mucosa, manifests as chronic inflammation. However, direct ratiometric visualization of SO2 in UC lesions has remained challenging due to the scarcity of ratiometric fluorescent probes with large emission shifts suitable for in vivo imaging. Herein, we present SL, a ratiometric fluorescent probe that reports SO2 via analyte-induced dual-emission rearrangement with a large spectral shift. Using SL, we captured dynamic SO2 signals at the cellular level and visualized endogenous SO2 changes in UC mice. These findings demonstrate that SL enables the examination of SO2 dynamics in living systems and may facilitate investigations of SO2-associated signaling events in inflammatory pathological contexts.

title: An engineered probiotic yeast converts extracellular ATP into adenosine to alleviate experimental colitis.
authors: Liu H, Zhang M, Wu W, Deng Q, Li X, Ma R, Bai L, Huang B
abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a chronic relapsing intestinal disorder characterized by mucosal inflammation, epithelial barrier disruption, and gut microbial dysbiosis. Excessive extracellular ATP (eATP) accumulates in inflamed intestinal tissues and amplifies immune activation through purinergic signaling, whereas adenosine generated from extracellular nucleotide metabolism exerts immunoregulatory effects. Here, we engineered the probiotic yeast Saccharomyces boulardii to sense eATP and convert it into adenosine through a CRISPR-engineered dual-enzyme pathway consisting of apyrase and 5'-nucleotidase. The engineered strain showed ATP-responsive pathway activation and efficiently generated adenosine from eATP, allowing extracellular nucleotide metabolism to be modulated in inflammatory settings. Oral administration of this strain significantly alleviated disease severity in acute dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced colitis and showed beneficial effects in a repeated-DSS model, improved barrier-related epithelial features, reduced pro-inflammatory cytokine production, and supported mucosal recovery. Integrated microbiome and transcriptome analyses further showed partial restoration of gut microbial community structure, partial recovery of predicted microbial purine-related pathways, and attenuation of mucosal T-cell activation. Together, these findings indicate that engineered Saccharomyces boulardii can regulate extracellular purine metabolism in the inflamed gut and provide a microbial strategy for modulating intestinal inflammation.

title: Qi Yin San Liang San prevents gefitinib-induced nociceptive hypersensitivity by modulating TRPV1 channel activity.
authors: Yan K, Guo PX, Liang QY, Xu PT, Jin T, Chen LY, Liang CB, Guo MY
abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Qi Yin San Liang San (QYSLS) is a traditional Chinese medicine formula used as an adjunctive therapy for malignant tumors, and has been reported to reduce treatment-related toxicities. Gefitinib-associated nociceptive hypersensitivity remains underrecognized, with its underlying causal mechanism poorly defined. It is unclear whether QYSLS can prevent gefitinib-evoked adverse effect and the underlying molecular mechanism remain unknown. AIM OF THE STUDY: To explore the molecular mechanism of gefitinib-provoked nociceptive hypersensitivity and evaluate the preventive effects of QYSLS, with specific investigation of TRPV1 channel activity and CGRP release from dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neuron under this pathological condition. METHODS: A mouse model of gefitinib-provoked nociceptive hypersensitivity was established. QYSLS protection was assessed via pain behavioral tests and DRG histopathology. RNA-seq and network pharmacology were used for target screening. Surface plasmon resonance (SPR), cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA) and molecular docking confirmed direct gefitinib-TRPV1 binding. Calcium imaging evaluated TRPV1 channel activity in primary DRG neurons and TRPV1-overexpressing cells. Trpv1-/- mice were used to validate its function. RT-qPCR, immunofluorescence staining and ELISA measured DRG TRPV1/CGRP expression and CGRP release. RESULTS: Gefitinib induced time-dependent declines in mechanical withdrawal thresholds (8.7% of the control at day 28) and thermal withdrawal latencies (55.3% of control at day 28), accompanied by DRG injury in mice. DRG RNA-seq revealed elevated Trpv1 transcripts levels and enrichment of ion channel pathways. Gefitinib triggered TRPV1-dependent elevation of intracellular Ca2+ signals in DRG nociceptive neurons. Calcium imaging, SPR, CETSA, molecular docking and site-directed mutagenesis showed that gefitinib directly activates TRPV1. Residue Y454 is critical for this effect, while it is dispensable for capsaicin-mediated TRPV1 activation, and this activation elicits significant Ca2+ influx, neuronal excitation, and increased CGRP in DRG neurons. Genetic deletion of Trpv1 largely restored pain thresholds and rescued gefitinib-caused neuropathic pain. Oral QYSLS alleviated gefitinib-evoked weight loss, DRG histological damage and nociceptive hypersensitivity (recovered to 50.5% of control for mechanical withdrawal thresholds, and 94.7% of control for thermal withdrawal latency at day 28), accompanied by reductions in gefitinib-triggered DRG TRPV1 and CGRP expression of ∼34.6% and ∼56.1%, respectively. Quercetin and ferulic acid, the key bioactive ingredients of QYSLS, can inhibit gefitinib-induced TRPV1 activation. The analgesic-protective effects of QYSLS were substantially blunted in Trpv1-/- mice. CONCLUSIONS: This work identifies a previously unrecognized mechanism: Gefitinib triggers nociceptive hypersensitivity via DRG TRPV1 direct activation. Residue Y454 is critical for gefitinib- but not capsaicin-evoked TRPV1 activation, and CGRP may act as a downstream effector. QYSLS prevents this nociceptive hypersensitivity largely through TRPV1.

title: Ethnopharmacological basis of Huangqin Tang in colorectal cancer: Repurposing a classical formula to overcome PD-1 resistance via lactylation blockade.
authors: Song L, Zhang X, Liu A, Li X, Chen P, Liu X, Zeng A
abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Huangqin Tang (HQT), documented in the Shanghan Lun, is traditionally prescribed for "dysenteric disorders" (Li Ji). Modern clinical studies confirm its efficacy against ulcerative colitis and colorectal cancer-associated inflammation, providing a verified traditional basis for investigating its immunomodulatory effects in colorectal malignancy. However, the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to investigate the regulatory role of lactate-induced protein lactylation in MIF-driven PD-1 resistance and to determine if HQT can reverse this phenotype through metabolic reprogramming. MATERIALS AND METHODS: CT26-bearing BALB/c mice were administered HQT intragastrically combined with intraperitoneal anti-PD-1 antibodies. Tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes were profiled by flow cytometry. Integrative transcriptomics and network pharmacology were utilized to screen candidate targets. LC-MS/MS-based lactylomic profiling identified specific modification sites. Lactate modulation assays, and site-directed mutagenesis (NF-κB1 K249R) coupled with rescue experiments were performed in vitro to validate the molecular cascade mechanistically. RESULTS: HQT synergized with anti-PD-1 to suppress tumor growth and prolong survival. This combination remodeled the immune microenvironment, increasing CD8+ T cells and M1-like macrophages while reducing M2 macrophages and MDSCs. Mechanistically, HQT inhibited tumor glycolysis and lactate production. Lactylomic analysis revealed that lactate induced NF-κB1 lysine 249 (K249) lactylation in CD4+ Tregs, driving MIF transcription. Introducing the K249R mutation abolished lactate-induced MIF expression and reversed immunosuppression. HQT effectively reduced NF-κB1 K249 lactylation, disrupting the MIF-driven feedback loop. CONCLUSION: NF-κB1 K249 lactylation acts as a critical post-translational switch linking tumor glycolysis to Treg-mediated immunosuppression. HQT overcomes PD-1 resistance by suppressing this axis. These findings support combining metabolic intervention with immunotherapy and highlight K249 lactylation as a potential biomarker for treatment response.

title: Exposure-informed deconstruction of Chaihu Shugan San links tetramethylpyrazine-paeoniflorin to PRKACA-related neurotrophic signaling and brain-gut pharmacology.
authors: Zhou R, Cai Z, Wang Y, Gao Z, Zhang H, Huang X
abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Chaihu Shugan San (CSS) is traditionally used for emotional constraint and digestive discomfort. Identifying botanical and constituent contributions to these coordinated actions could clarify its pharmacological basis. AIM OF THE STUDY: To identify an active reduced CSS preparation and investigate its constituent contributions and PRKACA-related signaling. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Botanical screening and recombination were conducted in chronic unpredictable mild stress rats. The selected combination, FCP (Aurantii Fructus, Chuanxiong Rhizoma and Paeoniae Radix Alba), was chemically characterized. Tetramethylpyrazine (TMP) and paeoniflorin (PF) were measured in plasma after single-dose CSS administration and tested at FCP constituent-equivalent oral doses. Hippocampal assays, Prkaca silencing in HT22 cells and JMV2959 co-treatment examined molecular and pharmacological responses. RESULTS: FCP showed the broadest behavioral and gastrointestinal activity among the reduced preparations tested. TMP/PF reproduced selected FCP-associated responses and increased hippocampal cAMP, PKA activity, BDNF, PSD95 and Synapsin-1. Prkaca silencing attenuated cellular neurotrophic and synaptic-protein responses to TMP/PF. Compared with TMP/PF alone, JMV2959 co-treatment reduced gastric emptying, intestinal transit, sucrose preference and hippocampal cAMP, PKA activity and BDNF, whereas plasma acyl-ghrelin and open-field distance did not differ significantly. CONCLUSIONS: FCP retained coordinated behavioral and gastrointestinal actions of CSS, while TMP/PF reproduced a defined component of this pharmacology. Convergent cellular and hippocampal findings support PRKACA-related signaling as a mechanistically relevant component of the constituent response.

title: Dendrobium officinale extract ameliorates Alzheimer's disease by modulating PI3K-AKT-mTOR pathway and autophagy-related processes: An integrated study combining feature-based molecular networking, network pharmacology and multi-omics.
authors: Fu J, Liang Z, Wang F, Xiong F, Wang X, Sun J, Zhan J, Hu K
abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a multifactorial neurodegenerative disorder with limited effective treatments. Dendrobium officinale Kimura & Migo (D. officinale) has been traditionally used for dementia, but its active constituents and mechanisms remain unclear. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to systematically characterize the chemical constituents of D. officinale extract (DOE) and elucidate its anti-AD mechanisms using an integrated pharmacological strategy. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The chemical composition of DOE was analyzed using UHPLC-Q-TOF/MS combined with feature-based molecular networking (FBMN). Target prediction and pathway analysis were performed using a network pharmacology approach. Therapeutic effects were evaluated in 5×FAD mice using behavioral and histopathological assays. Mechanistic validation was further conducted using transcriptomics, proteomics, qRT-PCR, Western blotting, and molecular docking. RESULTS: Sixty-five components were identified, with apigenin, naringenin, rutin and oxyresveratrol as major identified constituents. Integrated multi-omics and network pharmacology analyses highlighted the PI3K-AKT-mTOR pathway and autophagy-related processes as potential mechanisms underlying the anti-AD effects of DOE. In 5×FAD mice, DOE markedly improved cognitive deficits, alleviated hippocampal neuronal injury, reduced Aβ plaque deposition, and suppressed astrocytic and microglial activation. Mechanistically, DOE significantly downregulated the mRNA expression of Pi3k, Akt, and Mtor, reduced AKT and mTOR phosphorylation, and showed a trend toward decreased PI3K phosphorylation. DOE also reduced p62 accumulation and increased the LC3-II/LC3-I ratio, suggesting an improvement in autophagy-related processes. Molecular docking further demonstrated favorable binding affinities of major identified constituents toward key targets, particularly AKT1 and PIK3CA. CONCLUSION: DOE ameliorates AD-related pathological changes, potentially through modulation of the PI3K-AKT-mTOR pathway and improvement of autophagy-related processes. These findings provide experimental evidence supporting the potential of D. officinale as a multi-target therapeutic candidate for AD.

title: Cardioprotective effects of Xin-Shu-Ning tablets against myocardial ischemia: Involvement of protein kinase B-related signaling in apoptosis and pyroptosis.
authors: Liu Y, Liu X, Gu Y, Xu F, Chen Y, Su W, Ding S, Qian C
abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Xin-Shu-Ning Tablets (XSNT) are traditionally used to promote blood circulation and resolve blood stasis, including for coronary heart disease-associated angina. Their cardioprotective mechanisms and bioactive constituents remain unclear. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to evaluate the cardioprotection of XSNT against myocardial ischemia and to investigate its underlying mechanisms and candidate bioactive constituents. MATERIALS AND METHODS: XSNT was evaluated in myocardial infarction (MI) mice using echocardiography, biochemical assays, histopathology, Western blotting, and immunofluorescence. Proteomics and prior network pharmacology guided PI3K/AKT analysis. H9c2 cells underwent 8 h of oxygen-glucose deprivation (OGD), with MK-2206 used to assess AKT involvement. Molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, cellular thermal shift assays, and cellular experiments were used to evaluate the candidates. RESULTS: XSNT improved cardiac function and reduced myocardial injury in MI mice. Reduced TUNEL staining and changes in Bcl-2/Bax and cleaved caspase-3 supported attenuation of apoptosis, while reductions in inflammasome- and GSDMD-related proteins indicated decreased pyroptosis-related signaling. These effects accompanied increased AKT phosphorylation and reduced NF-κB activation. XSNT produced similar responses in OGD-challenged H9c2 cells, and MK-2206 partially attenuated these effects. Puerarin showed a potential interaction with AKT and reproduced some cellular effects of XSNT, which were also attenuated by MK-2206. CONCLUSION: XSNT attenuated myocardial injury and distinct apoptosis- and pyroptosis-related responses, with pharmacological evidence supporting AKT involvement. Puerarin represents a candidate bioactive constituent. This study has several limitations, including the unclear cellular sources of myocardial pyroptosis-related signals, the lack of genetic validation of AKT involvement, and the need for further confirmation in primary cardiomyocytes.

Regional and national burden and aetiologies of non-COVID lower respiratory infections in Latin America and the Caribbean, 1990-2023: a secondary analysis of the global burden of disease study 2023.
authors: Sanabria-Herrera N, Gutierrez VA, Martínez LF, Tellez-Barros DC, Hurtado JS, Serrano-Mayorga CC, Mougin V, Wool E
abstract: BACKGROUND: Lower respiratory tract infections (LRTIs) remain a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, disproportionately affecting low- and middle-income regions. Reliable, up-to-date burden estimates are needed to inform public health strategies in Latin America and the Caribbean, where prevention and management strategies remain heterogeneous. We aimed to characterise temporal and geographical patterns in LRTI mortality, incidence, disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs), and aetiology across the region from 1990 to 2023. METHODS: We analysed secondary, modelled estimates of mortality, incidence, and DALYs attributable to LRTIs in Latin America and the Caribbean from 1990 to 2023, extracted from the GBD 2023 Results Tool and produced following the standardised GBD protocol coordinated by the Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation (IHME). FINDINGS: In Latin America and the Caribbean, LRTI mortality declined in most countries between 1990 and 2023, with the steepest reductions among children younger than five years (e.g., Brazil ARC -6·16, 95% UI -6·61 to -5·71). All-age mortality rose in some countries, but age-standardised rates showed that these increases reflected population ageing rather than rising age-specific risk. Following a sustained pre-pandemic decline, incidence showed and overall upward direction in the post-pandemic period across age groups, although the magnitude and statistical relevance of these changes varied by age and country, with the largest increase observed among children in Suriname (ARC +8·84, 95% UI +2·80 to +14·95). Streptococcus pneumoniae remained the leading cause of LRTI mortality in 2023 (7·68 per 100,000, 95% UI 7·11-8·24; ARC -2·70, 95% UI -2·96 to -2·45). INTERPRETATION: LRTIs remain a major cause of death in the region, with substantial progress among children but persistent burden among older adults, driven by population ageing, and evidence of a post-pandemic increase in incidence. There is a great importance of combining clinical interventions with broader public health strategies addressing vaccination coverage, antimicrobial-resistance surveillance, nutrition, housing, and access to primary care, particularly in populations that have experienced less favourable trends. FUNDING: Wellcome Trust (303666/Z/23/Z); UK International Development (301542-403); the Gates Foundation (INV-063472) and Universidad de La Sabana (MED-289-2020).

title: Oral and anal detection of Treponema pallidum DNA among transgender women and travestis with high-titre syphilis in Brazil: findings from the MyTTrA study.
authors: Salle R, McCartney DJ, Grange PA, Mee P, Costa S, Magno L, Berçot B, de Sousa Mascena Veras MA
abstract: BACKGROUND: Data on transgender women and travestis (TGW) concerning oral and anal detection of Treponema pallidum (TP) DNA are lacking. We aimed to estimate the prevalence of oral and anal TP DNA detection and the frequency of azithromycin resistance-associated mutations among TGW with high-titre syphilis in Brazil. METHODS: We conducted a nested cross-sectional study as part of the TransOdara study among TGW in five Brazilian cities. Participants with high-titre syphilis (reactive treponemal test and VDRL titre ≥1:8) and an analysable oral or anal specimen underwent quantitative PCR targeting the tpp47 and polA genes to detect TP DNA. TP DNA-positive specimens were further analysed using nested PCR and Sanger sequencing to identify mutations associated with azithromycin resistance. FINDINGS: Among the 249 participants with high-titre serological syphilis and analysable sample, TP DNA was detected in 25 (10.0%, 95% CI 6.6-14.5): 14 (5.6%) from the oral site only, 6 (2.4%) from the anal site only, and 5 (2.0%) from both sites. Participants in whom TP DNA was detected were younger and more frequently reported STI symptoms and anogenital ulcers during the preceding six months. The detection rate increased with VDRL titre (odds ratio 2.44, 95% CI 1.74-3.41 per doubling of titre for any oral or anal detection). Mutations associated with azithromycin resistance were observed in 76% (19/25, 95% CI 54.9-90.6) of participants in whom TP was detected. INTERPRETATION: TP DNA was detected in 10% of participants with high-titre serological syphilis. Detection increased with higher VDRL titres, supporting an association between higher non-treponemal titres and mucosal TP DNA detection. These findings support continued epidemiological and molecular surveillance of syphilis and of azithromycin resistance in transgender populations. They do not support site-specific PCR screening: syphilis diagnosis remains serological, and benzathine benzylpenicillin G remains the treatment of choice. FUNDING: French National Agency for Research on AIDS, Viral Hepatitis, and Emerging Infectious Diseases (ANRS/MIE).

title: Calibrating public genome archives for AMR surveillance: Four decades of redundancy-aware phylogenomics of pandemic Escherichia coli ST131.
authors: White RT, Biggs PJ, Burgess SA, Collis RM, Cookson AL, Downing T, Elvy J, Featherstone LA
journal: Drug resistance updates : reviews and commentaries in antimicrobial and anticancer chemotherapy
abstract: AIMS: Escherichia coli sequence type (ST)131 is a globally disseminated multidrug-resistant pathogen, yet public genome collections are skewed by uneven sampling and repeated sequencing of genetically near-identical isolates. Rather than another reconstruction of ST131 evolution, we quantified redundancy, reassessed population structure, and tested how sampling bias affects estimates of phylogenetic diversity, clade-specific dating, and fluoroquinolone-resistance-associated diversification. METHODS: EnteroBase core-genome multilocus sequence typing (cgMLST) hierarchical clustering was used to reduce redundancy among 16,713 public ST131 complex genomes. Representative public genomes were combined with 390 unpublished New Zealand ST131 surveillance genomes from 1999 to 2019. Clade-specific phylogenetic and temporal analyses were performed for Clades A, B, and C, with sensitivity analyses using stricter cgMLST clustering and phylogenetic-diversity-guided subsampling. RESULTS: Public genomes were highly redundant: just 2/409 cgMLST groups contained 85.2% of public genomes. After redundancy reduction, dated Clades A, B, and C phylogenies spanning 1999-2023 (n = 113), 1982-2025 (n = 240), and 1999-2025 (n = 614), respectively, were constructed. Clades A and B showed distinct temporal histories and evolutionary rates. Date-randomization supported temporal information in Clade C, although incomplete convergence of the observed-date relaxed-clock and Bayesian Skyline analyses means that exact Clade C molecular-date and demographic estimates should be interpreted cautiously. The broad Clade C reconstruction nevertheless indicated expansion of the dominant fluoroquinolone-resistant lineage in the late 1990s/early 2000s and again in the mid-2000s. CONCLUSIONS: Public ST131 datasets reflect sampling distribution as well as number of available genomes. Redundancy in dominant cgMLST groups can obscure uncommon lineages and blur emergence with later expansion. In Clade C, redundancy-aware analysis was broadly consistent with previous estimates placing major fluoroquinolone-resistant diversification in the early 1990s, while indicating that early resistance diversification preceded later amplification of resistant sublineages.

title: Proceedings of the 3rd edition of the International e-Health Forum 2024.
Cortical spreading depression on Riemannian 2-manifolds: eikonal-curvature analysis and sulcal trapping.
authors: Enver A, Tepe N, Sara MY, Dilekoz E, Bolay H
abstract: Cortical spreading depression (CSD) is a slowly propagating wave of near-complete neuronal depolarization underlying migraine aura and implicated in stroke, traumatic brain injury, and subarachnoid hemorrhage. Existing reaction-diffusion models of CSD treat the cortex as a flat Euclidean domain, ignoring its highly folded, individually variable geometry. We develop a fully covariant FitzHugh-Nagumo (FHN) reaction-diffusion system on a smooth compact Riemannian 2-manifold [Formula: see text] representing the cortical sheet, in which the Euclidean Laplacian is replaced by the Laplace-Beltrami operator [Formula: see text]. Three mathematical results are established: (i) local and global well-posedness in [Formula: see text] together with positive invariance of the physiological region via parabolic semigroup theory; (ii) a curvature-corrected eikonal relation [Formula: see text], in which the wavefront speed is modulated by the geodesic curvature of the front; and (iii) a sulcal-trapping theorem giving an explicit criterion under which an excitable wave entering a sulcus (negative Gauss curvature region) remains confined to it. Numerically, we develop two complementary solvers: a discrete exterior calculus (DEC) scheme on triangulated surfaces using the cotangent Laplacian with implicit-explicit (IMEX) time-stepping, and a physics-informed neural network (PINN) surrogate that evaluates [Formula: see text] via the closest-point projection of the ambient Euclidean Laplacian. The PINN framework supports both forward simulation and the inverse identification of excitability fields from sparse observations, and a noise-ablation study quantifies its practical identifiability. The parameters of the slow subsystem and of the coupling functions are inherited from our published, cohort-calibrated thalamocortical model, which was calibrated against 67 paired-pulse somatosensory evoked potential (SEP) recordings from nine analysable animals of a cohort of 14 male Wistar rats (1, 233 sweeps) acquired in the Neuroscience Laboratory of Gazi University, with CSD induced by topical KCl application. We validate convergence on [Formula: see text] with the spectral ground-truth [Formula: see text], exhibit a propagating ring wave with a refractory tail, and verify the eikonal-curvature prediction across two orders of magnitude in geodesic curvature, including the leading correction due to the recovery variable; a mesh-convergence study yields explicit resolution requirements for evaluating the trapping criterion on MRI-derived cortical surfaces.

title: Rehospitalizations after acute myocardial infarction in patients diagnosed by coronary angiography - the MADDEC study.
authors: Aitokari LJ, Vuorinen J, Hernesniemi J
abstract: Objectives. The rate of rehospitalizations and fatal adverse events after myocardial infarction (MI) is reportedly high in previous studies and reducing these events is considered an important goal. This study aimed to clarify the rate of serious events leading to hospitalization or death after invasively managed MI in a contemporary setting. Design. In a retrospective registry study, the rate of serious adverse events leading to rehospitalizations or death during the first year after MI was examined from Tampere University hospital records. Study population consisted of all consecutive MI patients who underwent coronary angiography at Tays Heart Hospital between 2012 and 2016. This study focused on bleeding events, cerebrovascular events, exacerbation of heart failure, recurrent MI and unstable angina pectoris leading to rehospitalization. Results. During the five-year period, 2904 consecutive patients were treated for MI and successfully discharged or transferred to a primary health care unit (95.5% of all patients). 4.8% of these patients died during the first year after MI with 66.2% of all deaths due to cardiac causes, fatal bleeds, infections, or cerebrovascular events. Of all patients, 17.8% were rehospitalized for these causes and adding events leading to death without rehospitalization, the rate of serious events was 18.8%. Age but not sex, associated significantly with the rate of serious adverse events with the cumulative incidence exceeding 20% in patients aged 70-79 years and reaching 29% in patients ≥80 years. Conclusions. Cause-specific rehospitalization rates were low, but highly dependent on age.

title: Circulating LRG1 in heart failure: association with type 2 diabetes and antidiabetic therapy class.
authors: Alrosan K, Odeh M, Alqudah A, Abudalo R, Qnais E
journal: Journal of diabetes and metabolic disorders
abstract: BACKGROUND: Heart failure (HF) and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) frequently coexist and share remodelling and inflammatory mechanisms. Although leucine-rich α-2 glycoprotein 1 (LRG1) has been identified as a biomarker associated with vascular remodelling, fibrosis, and inflammation, its role in HF patients with type 2 diabetes and its connection to antidiabetic treatments remains unclear. METHODS: 115 patients with HF were divided into three groups for this cross-sectional study: HF who had no previously documented diagnosis of diabetes mellitus and were not receiving antidiabetic medication at enrolment (n = 42), HF with T2DM treated with DPP-4 inhibitors (n = 35), and HF with T2DM treated with SGLT-2 inhibitors (n = 38). The groups' clinical characteristics, metabolic parameters, and circulating LRG1 levels were compared. RESULTS: LRG1 levels differed significantly across the groups (p = 0.002), with the lowest levels observed in the SGLT-2 inhibitor group. A post hoc analysis revealed a significant difference between the SGLT-2 inhibitor group and group of no previously documented diagnosis of diabetes mellitus (p = 0.001). No significant correlations were observed between LRG1 and clinical or metabolic variables. CONCLUSION: Circulating LRG1 levels in HF patients differed between study groups, with the lowest levels observed in the SGLT-2 inhibitor group. These findings suggest an association between treatment group and LRG1 levels, but the cross-sectional design precludes causal inference regarding the effects of antidiabetic medications on inflammatory and remodelling pathways.

title: Atomically dispersed nanoactivators drive innate mitochondrial biogenesis for active neuroprotection in ischemic stroke.
authors: Liu M, Lin M, Chen M, Huang Q, Xia C, Chen L, Chen Y, Zhang J
abstract: Mitigating mitochondrial bioenergetic failure is a pivotal yet formidable neuroprotective goal in treating cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI). However, conventional pharmacological interventions remain largely confined to passive antioxidant defense, which temporarily scavenges reactive oxygen species (ROS) without restoring organelle function. Here, we report a bimetallic nanoactivator (RMV) designed to drive active mitochondrial revival for rescuing ischemic tissues. RMV comprises atomically dispersed ruthenium sites anchored within an oxygen-deficient manganese hydroxide matrix via synergistic Ru-O-Mn bridges. Benefiting from its intrinsic mitochondriotropic properties, RMV effectively intercepts aberrant electron leakage and breaks the self-amplifying cycle of ROS-induced ROS release through cascade multi-enzyme mimetic activities. Importantly, transcriptomic profiling and ultrastructural analysis reveal that RMV transcends passive antioxidant defense by functioning as a bioactive switch. It revives the suppressed SIRT1-PGC1α-TFAM signaling axis, fundamentally driving mitochondrial biogenesis and the reconstruction of functionally intact respiratory chains. In a murine stroke model, RMV treatment induces a 1.52-fold expansion of the neuronal mitochondrial biomass under ischemic stress, thereby suppressing neuronal apoptosis, reducing infarct volumes, and favorably reshaping an M2-polarized neuroimmune microenvironment. These integrated effects yield robust and sustained neurofunctional recovery. Our study shifts the neuroprotective paradigm from reactive damage control to active mitochondrial biogenesis, offering an atomically engineered strategy for ischemic stroke management.

Defect-engineered piezoelectric heterointerfaces enable ultrasound-amplified built-in electric fields for bacterial envelope destabilization and implant infection control.
authors: Liu P, Lu S, Chen J, Cheng H, Yan J, Yao X, Wang G, Zhang X
abstract: Built-in electric fields (BIEFs) at piezoelectric heterointerfaces are widely invoked to assist charge separation, but their contribution to antibacterial activity under ultrasound remains poorly understood. Here, we develop a defect-engineered piezoelectric heterointerface strategy to investigate BIEF-related interfacial electrical effects. Density functional theory (DFT)-guided screening identifies a dual-vacancy piezoelectric heterojunction (BTO3-X/MoS2-X) with enhanced interfacial polarization. Under ultrasound, BTO3-X/MoS2-X efficiently kills Staphylococcus aureus, accompanied by pronounced bacterial envelope destabilization. This response is accompanied by membrane lipid perturbation, increased permeability, respiratory inhibition, and intracellular ROS accumulation. GROMACS simulations show that a model lipid bilayer destabilizes only under a sufficiently strong applied electric field. In infected implant models, ultrasound activated BTO3-X/MoS2-X reduces early peri-implant bacterial burden and promotes a repair-favorable inflammatory microenvironment. These findings highlight the potential contribution of BIEF-related interfacial electrical effects to ultrasound responsive antibacterial activity and offer a defect-engineering strategy for implant infection control.

title: Mechanisms underlying the effects of Buyang Huanwu Decoction against sepsis-induced ARDS using network pharmacology and experimental validation.
authors: Tan W, Wang C, Liu X, Deng J, Sang Z, Hu X
abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Buyang Huanwu Decoction (BYHW), a classic formula from Yilin Gaicuo Qing Dynasty, is indicated for stroke in patients with qi deficiency and blood stasis in the Chinese Pharmacopoeia. In traditional Chinese medicine (TCM), the pathogenesis of acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is associated with qi deficiency, blood stasis, and heat-toxin obstructing the lungs, which align with the therapeutic actions of this formula. AIM OF THE STUDY: To investigate the effects of BYHW on sepsis-induced ARDS and the mechanisms underlying these effects. MATERIALS AND METHODS: ARDS was induced through LPS treatment in wild-type and eNOS-deficient (eNOS-/-) mice. The components of BYHW were analyzed using UPLC-UV-MS. Potential associated targets and pathways were predicted by network pharmacology and molecular docking experiments. Relevant protein and mRNA expression levels were assessed by Western blot analysis, immunofluorescence analysis, or qPCR. RESULTS: BYHW significantly improving the hypothermia, elevated plasma levels of IL-1β, TNF-α, and IL-6, the lung index and injury induced by LPS in wild-type (WT) mice. However, these effects of BYHW were markedly in eNOS-/- mice. LPS downregulated AQP1 protein expression and upregulated Cav-1 protein expression and the p-P65/P65 ratio in both groups but increased the p-IκB/IκB ratio only in the WT mice. Pretreatment of BYHW increased the expression of eNOS and AQP1, decreased the Cav-1 expression and P65/IκB phosphorylation in WT mice, but the action on the P65/IκB phosphorylation and AQP1 expression were abrogated in eNOS-/- mice. CONCLUSION: BYHW protect against sepsis-induced ARDS may be related to decrease the eNOS-NF-κB-mediated synthesis of inflammatory cytokines and upregulation of AQP1 expression.

title: A mitochondria-targeting dual-emissive probe for imaging hypoxia-associated biomarkers in early non-alcoholic fatty liver disease.
authors: Zhou X, Gu R, Zou Y, Rajalakshmi K, Lee DK, Song JW, Nam YS, Zhu D
journal: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy
abstract: Hypoxia, characterized by a deficiency of oxygen, is associated with the progression of various diseases and the formation of solid tumors. Prolonged hypoxia increases mitochondrial viscosity and induces mitochondrial autophagy, making these important biomarkers of hypoxic conditions. Herein, we developed MI-NO2, a dual-responsive fluorescent probe for the simultaneous detection of nitroreductase (NTR) activity and viscosity. Upon enzymatic reduction by NTR, MI-NO2 is converted to MI, resulting in enhanced intramolecular charge transfer (ICT) and a fluorescence turn-on response in the green channel. The sensing mechanism was confirmed by 1H NMR, HR-MS, HPLC, and DFT calculations. In addition, MI-NO2 exhibited enhanced fluorescence in the yellow channel under high-viscosity conditions owing to suppression of the twisted ICT (TICT) process. The probe successfully visualized mitochondrial hypoxia in living cells and distinguished hypoxic from normoxic conditions. Moreover, MI-NO2 enabled monitoring of hypoxia and the associated increase in viscosity increase in an early-stage mouse model of non-alcoholic fatty liver disease. Importantly, the probe facilitated the sequential detection of hypoxia-related biomarkers, namely NTR activity and viscosity, using separate fluorescence channels without spectral cross-talk. MI-NO2 therefore provides an imaging platform for the early diagnosis of hypoxia-associated diseases.

title: Hepatic ITGBL1 promotes fibrogenesis and ductular remodeling through integrin-dependent latent TGF-β activation.
authors: He MK, Chen YH, Chen KC, Huang CT, Tang CC, Yang DJ, Lee CH, Hsu CC
journal: Biochimica et biophysica acta. Molecular basis of disease
abstract: Liver fibrosis is a major determinant of chronic liver disease progression and hepatobiliary remodeling. However, extracellular regulators linking fibrogenesis to pathological biliary responses remain incompletely understood. Integrin beta-like protein 1 (ITGBL1) is an extracellular matrix-associated protein implicated in integrin modulation, but its functional role in chronic liver injury remains unclear. A liver-specific doxycycline (DOX)-inducible zebrafish model was established to evaluate the effects of hepatic ITGBL1 gain-of-function in vivo. Fibrogenic and biliary responses were assessed using histologic, molecular, and genetic approaches. Mechanistic studies tested pathway dependence on itgav and ltbp1 using liver-specific genetic ablation, with cilengitide used as a complementary RGD-integrin pharmacologic perturbation. Hepatocyte-specific ITGBL1 induction triggered progressive hepatic stellate cell activation, extracellular matrix accumulation, and chronic fibrotic remodeling. Sustained ITGBL1 expression further promoted ductular reaction and biliary epithelial expansion during chronic liver injury progression. Genetic disruption of itgav or ltbp1 attenuated SMAD3 activation, collagen deposition, fibrogenic transcriptional programs, and associated histological remodeling; cilengitide independently attenuated fibrogenic readouts. These data support a working model in which hepatic ITGBL1 lies upstream of integrin/LTBP1-dependent latent TGF-β/SMAD3 signaling and provide a mechanistic framework for further resolving the molecular interactions among ITGBL1, ITGAV, and LTBP1 and the αv-integrin heterodimer involved. This pathway may represent a therapeutic target for fibrosis-associated biliary remodeling.
